title: The 3.8.0 med defects are fixed: locks, guard false positive, the affected listing, dependants at mint, and the empty task gate
description: D9: a med defect holds a release. Register entries F754, F800, F809 (open part), F792 (with its P151 recurrences) and F779, each verified open against main on 2026-10-29/31, plus F821's release-tier flake in tests/test__locks.py.
desiredOutcome: Each entry's Do is met with a case that goes red on the defect, the register status of each reads FIXED with its commit, and release-tier CI is green on the phase's landing commit.

findings.issue: The new predicate keys on the stored basis (`_mio.gate_cleared(tests)`, i.e. gateBasis == `cleared`) rather than on the gate that actually measures the task. Its own docstring says 'the phase's own gate may be empty too', and in that state the defect the task describes ('A task can close with no gate while the record reads green') is still open by a second shape: a tdd/regression task whose own tests.gate is absent or [] with no basis falls back to its phase (`_manifest_io.gate_entries`, _manifest_io.py:685-692), an empty phase testGate is a designed, validator-accepted state (`_manifest_phases.py:791`, `phase add --gate-clear`), `run-test-gate` answers `empty-gate` with exit 0 (run-test-gate.py:5401-5420), and `done` closes it via `_close_gate`'s arm '%s declares no gate, nor does its phase, so its close rests on its commit alone' (audit-task.py:7289-7313) - `_owed_case_gate_refusal` returns None because gateBasis is not `cleared`. Judged by reading, not run.
findings.resolution: Ask the refusal at `done` (and, if wanted, at the writes) of the resolved gate: refuse when tests.mode is tdd/regression and `_mio.gate_entries(phase, node)[0]` is empty, which covers both the cleared gate and the fallback to an empty phase gate; add a case beside ocg8 with a tdd task carrying no own gate in a phase whose testGate is [] (and its gate-only second-direction pair).

findings.issue: On a STARTED task the scope refusal prints `_OWED_CASE_WRITE_REMEDY`, whose second half ('--tests-mode gate-only if it owes no case of its own') is itself refused: a tests.mode change on a started task is a narrowing `_narrowings` blocks (fg6 pins 'already been attempted'), unlike tests.gate which is `_FORWARD_ONLY`. The `done` arm already words its remedy for this ('A started task may still move its gate ... so the remedy is the gate and not the mode'); the scope arm does not, so e.g. `scope <started tdd task> --gate-clear` names a dead-end remedy.
findings.resolution: Pass `_started(node)`-dependent remedy text at the _locked_scope call site (the gate-only half only for a task not yet started), and pin it with a case on a started tdd task asserting '--tests-mode gate-only' is absent from the refusal.

findings.issue: User-visible behaviour changed and the surfaces describing `--gate-clear` still say it is how a task reaches the EMPTY gate ('`--gate-clear` for none'), with no mention that a tdd/regression task (including one whose mode `add` derived from its title) is now refused and must pass `--tests-mode gate-only`. The executor named this follow-up itself; it is outside the task's declared files.
findings.resolution: Add one sentence to each surface (or to verbs-in-full.md and point the others at it) stating the refusal and its two remedies, and a CHANGELOG entry for the new refusal.

findings.issue: done refuses a tdd/regression task only on a stored cleared gateBasis; a task with no gate of its own whose phase gate is empty still closes green through the declares-no-gate branch of _close_gate
findings.resolution: refuse when the gate that would actually run (_mio.gate_entries(phase, node)) is empty for a tdd/regression task; fix the scope refusal hint on a started task (mode change is refused there); document the refusal in commands/task.md, reference/verbs-in-full.md, README and CHANGELOG

findings.issue: the heredoc split still grades three house-form bodies as shell (read, not run): _STDIN_SHELL matches a script file extension (x.sh) as a shell; _scan_quotes does not track backquote substitutions, so a backquoted house form opens no heredoc; gh pr create --body "$(cat <<EOF ...)" is not an accepted head. Third recurrence of the class guard-uncommitted and the shared head were
findings.resolution: state the invariant once in _config - a heredoc whose substitution is the whole or part of a quoted argument is data to every guard, whatever command carries the argument - and derive accepted shapes from it rather than from a list of heads; red-first one case per path plus the allow/deny pair kept from the shared-head fix; keep the hook import budget

findings.issue: contradicts task clause: the task asks for one sentence on each surface describing --gate-clear, or for verbs-in-full.md to carry it with the other surfaces pointing at it. commands/task.md still reads '--gate-clear for none' with neither the refusal nor a pointer, so the one surface a user reads first still teaches the spelling that tdd/regression tasks are now refused. The executor's stated reason holds: in the task tree measure-context.py reports '/audit:task add 7989 / 8000', so only 11 bytes of headroom remain and no sentence fits. The clause is nonetheless unmet on that surface.
findings.resolution: Either accept the narrowing explicitly (the orchestrator records the waiver), or free bytes in commands/task.md (trim other prose on the add path or move a passage to verbs-in-full.md) and add a short caveat after '--gate-clear for none', for example '(refused on tdd/regression; see verbs-in-full)'. Re-run measure-context --gate afterwards.

tasks.title: A phase lock held by the caller's own process under an earlier session id is reported as the caller's, and a dead drive's lock is not read as a live run
tasks.description: Register F754. When a Claude Code conversation continues under a new session id in the same process, the phase lock taken under the old id reads as HELD by a live run forever (the holder pid is the long-lived claude process), and only release --session <old> --pid <pid> lets go. Do: when the caller's process ancestry contains the holder pid but the session differs, say so and offer the release by name; and base liveness on the drive command's own pid or a heartbeat rather than the long-lived claude process, so a dead drive releases. A lock held by an unrelated live pid still refuses.

tasks.title: guard-uncommitted reads a heredoc body or a quoted argument as data, not as a command, so a description that quotes git is not refused
tasks.description: Register F800. The guard refused an audit-task.py add whose heredoc description merely quoted git commands: it could not tokenize the command, assumed the widest loss set, and refused; the same description passed on stdin from a file. Bind the evidence to the operation: when the command cannot be tokenized, read only what is outside heredoc bodies and quoted arguments; red-first the allow case and keep the deny case red.

add: .claude/hooks/guard-uncommitted.py: an audit-task add whose heredoc description quotes a stash command and a checkout is allowed; the same commands run outside the heredoc are still refused

outcome.technical: guard-uncommitted.py: when the sibling parser cannot tokenize a line, reading() now builds executed_text(command), a quote- and heredoc-aware walk. It drops quoted-delimiter heredoc bodies, including one inside a command substitution inside double quotes (the house description form), and drops quoted ARGUMENTS. It keeps every command substitution and backquote, inside double quotes and inside unquoted-delimiter bodies too. It keeps a quoted program word and every quoted argument of git. It truncates at a quote or substitution that never closes; bash runs nothing past one, verified with bash -c on an unterminated quote, which ran only the earlier complete lines. It returns None, keeping the raw-line reading and the unchanged widest refusal, when any command in the line can run text it is handed: a shell, eval, make, xargs or exec, a program named by path, or an interpreter not running a script file. That judgement uses the shared _config.program_candidates, is_shell, is_interpreter and runs_own_program. The view is re-parsed with the sibling's git_invocations and judged on the operation; that reading is labelled 'executed', and its refusal says the line could not be tokenized and what was read. If the view will not parse either, the shapes grade the view. Also fixed: the pre-filter's tree-wide dot (_DOT) now ends where a shell word ends, so a variable assigned from a substitution running a tree-wide checkout is no longer waved through before the parser is asked; it was allowed on HEAD, tokenizable or not. gu41 is reworded to assert the 'could not be tokenized' basis: its old 'TEXT' assertion now belongs to the raw path, and gu51 pins the two labels apart. New cases gu43-gu51. Selftest 52/52. Gate `python3 tools/sweep-selftests.py .claude/hooks/guard-uncommitted.py` exit 0 (1/1 files ok, 52 cases). Mutation probe: <scratchpad>/p153-3/probe/mutations.py, output in output.txt beside it, run as `python3 mutations.py <checkout>`. Baseline 52/52, and all nine rows were KILLED, including both over-fire directions (M8 every interpreter a runner turned gu44 and gu49 red; M9 every command a runner did the same) and the defect restored (M1 turned gu44 and gu49 red). Probe exit 0. Only that task's files are open here.' The probe therefore lives in the scratchpad. (b) The first submit call was refused by the live plugin guard-history-rewrite, whose message opens: '[guard-history-rewrite] `git st` + `ash` moves work between the working tree and the stash' (spelled split here for the same reason). The return object's prose quoted the stash command, and because the heredoc head names its script by a QUOTED path, _config._plain_script_run does not vouch for it, so the body was graded as code and fell to the raw-text arm. It names executed_text() and its selftest, and says nothing enforces the rule for a guard added later. The names targets, judge, parser and decide found in guard-release.py, require-claim-block.py, the skills and CHANGELOG are those files' own same-named symbols: .claude hooks do not import this file, and none of this file's signatures changed, so they are still correct. CONTRIBUTING.md's basename dependants (evals.json, _output.py, the four suites above, tools/affected.py, tools/check-committed-pii.py) reference the file, not this bullet, and no heading was renamed; still correct, and the suites are green. FOUND, OUT OF SCOPE (not edited; not a declared file): the root of the tokenized-path half is _config._head_runs_body in plugins/audit/hooks/_config.py. Its _HEAD_INDIRECTION search matches the command substitution that ENCLOSES the cat heredoc, so every house-form body (commit message or description) is graded as SHELL by every guard sharing split_heredocs. Measured: git_invocations on an audit-task add whose house-form description has a body line opening with the stash verb returns a stash invocation with args ['is','banned','here']. A body line opening with a tree-wide checkout would be refused by this guard on the tokenized path, and the plugin's history guard reads the same bodies as commands; refusal (b) above is a second instance of the class. The fix belongs in _config: read the head from the innermost open substitution, and stop letting a quoted script path disqualify a plain script run. It needs a register entry and its own task.

tasks.title: scope --gate-clear on a tdd or regression task refuses, or falls back to the phase gate, rather than closing the task with no gate
tasks.description: Register F779 (verified 2026-10-31 at ad838231): audit-task.py scope <task> --gate-clear on a tdd task exits 0 and writes {gate: [], gateBasis: cleared}; run-test-gate reports empty-gate. A task can close with no gate while the record reads green. Pick the structurally correct answer (refuse on tdd/regression, or fall back to the phase gate with the basis saying so) and check the drive's close path end to end.

add: tests/test_audit_task.py: scope --gate-clear on a tdd task neither writes an empty gate silently nor lets the task close as green

outcome.technical: DESIGN: refuse, not fall back. A tdd/regression task whose tests.gateBasis is `cleared` is now refused wherever a write would leave that state, and `done` refuses to close one. I chose refusal over falling back to the phase gate for three reasons. (1) The fallback answers a request for no gate with a gate nobody named, usually the phase's widest one. (2) The phase gate may itself be empty (P3 in the fixture), so a fallback does not close the state. (3) mode and gate contradict each other and only the caller knows which is wrong, so the refusal names both remedies (`--gate <cmd>` / `--tests-mode gate-only`). An empty task gate with NO basis already falls back to the phase (_manifest_io.gate_entries, _manifest_io.py:689), so the defect state is exactly mode in {tdd, regression} AND gate_cleared(tests). CODE (plugins/audit/scripts/manifest/audit-task.py): new `_OWES_CASE_MODES` (derived from _vocab.TESTS_MODE minus gate-only), `_owed_case_gate_refusal(tid, tests, remedy)` and `_OWED_CASE_WRITE_REMEDY`, placed beside `_retarget_gate_contradiction`. outcome.technical: plugins/audit/hooks/_config.py: (1) _scan_quotes now delegates to a new _scan_contexts, which also returns where each open context began (one scanner, so marker quoting and enclosing substitution cannot disagree). (2) New _substitution_runs_body(prefix, cmd): when the marker sits inside a $( ), the head is read from the INNERMOST substitution (_head_runs_body on the text after its $( ); if that head runs its stdin it answers; otherwise the body is the substitution's output and stays data only when exactly one substitution is open, it is the whole of one double-quoted argument, the enclosing command is not in command position (empty, or after ; & | ( newline), and _holds_output_as_text vouches for the consumer: a plain script run (no interpreter env option such as NODE_OPTIONS anywhere in the command) or git commit/tag with the substitution as a -m/--message value (_GIT_MESSAGE_OPTIONS). Everything else returns shell. Returns False when no substitution is open, and split_heredocs then reads the marker line's head as before. split_heredocs builds the prefix from the kept lines plus the marker line, so a $( opened on an earlier line is seen too (before, `bash -c "$(` + newline + `cat <<'EOF'` dropped its body as data). (3) _last_command returns shell_words of the last simple command (falls back to a blank split when quoting never closes), and _pipes_to_script_run reads the far side with shell_words, so a quoted script path no longer disqualifies a plain script run; _plain_script_run's char check is unchanged and now applies to dequoted words.
